questions.question_text: What is the parametric form of the line $3x - 2y + 6 = 0$ when using $x = 2t$?

options.why: Made a sign error when moving the constant term $+6$ to the other side.
Forgot to divide the right-hand side by the coefficient $2$ of $y$.
Substituted $t$ instead of $2t$ into the $3x$ term.

questions.question_text: What is the parametric form of the line $4x + 5y - 20 = 0$ when using $x = 5t - 5$?

options.why: Added $-20$ and $-20$ to get $0$ instead of moving $-40$ to the right-hand side.
Failed to change the sign of $20t$ when moving it across the equals sign.
Forgot to divide through by $5$ to make $y$ the subject.

questions.question_text: Express $y = x^2 - 4x + 7$ in parametric form using $x = t + 2$.

options.why: Expanded $(t+2)^2$ as $t^2+4$ and forgot $-4(t+2)$ terms.
Failed to distribute the negative sign in $-4(t+2)$.
Subtracted $8$ from $7$ but forgot the $+4$ from expanding the square.

questions.question_text: Express the parabola $x^2 = 12(y - 1)$ in parametric form using $x = 6t$.

options.why: Subtracted $1$ instead of adding $1$ when making $y$ the subject.
Divided $6$ by $12$ instead of squaring $6$ first to get $36/12=3$.
Forgot to divide $36t^2$ by the factor of $12$.

questions.question_text: Which pair of parametric equations expresses the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 64$ with parameter $\theta$?

options.why: Used $r^2=64$ as the coefficient instead of taking the square root $r=8$.
Squared the trigonometric functions instead of using standard linear forms.
Used cosine for both coordinates instead of sine for the $y$-coordinate.

questions.question_text: Express the circle $(x + 5)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = 36$ in parametric form with parameter $\theta$.

options.why: Read the centre straight off the brackets as $(5, -1)$ instead of flipping each sign to get $(-5, 1)$.
Took the right-hand side $36$ as the radius instead of taking $r = \sqrt{36} = 6$.
Read the centre straight off the brackets as $(5, -1)$ and also used $36$ as the radius instead of $r = \sqrt{36} = 6$.

questions.solution_text:
Centre is $(a, b) = (-5, 1)$ and radius is $r = \sqrt{36} = 6$.
$x = -5 + 6\cos\theta,\; y = 1 + 6\sin\theta$

questions.question_text: Express the circle $x^2 + y^2 - 8x - 4y - 5 = 0$ in parametric form with parameter $\theta$.

options.why: Read the centre as $(-4, -2)$ straight from the minus signs inside $(x - 4)^2$ and $(y - 2)^2$ instead of $(4, 2)$.
Used the right-hand side $r^2 = 25$ as the radius rather than taking $r = \sqrt{25} = 5$.
Read the centre as $(-4, -2)$ from the minus signs in the brackets and also used $r^2 = 25$ as the radius instead of $r = 5$.

questions.question_text: Express the circle $x^2 + y^2 + 6x - 10y + 9 = 0$ in parametric form with parameter $\theta$.

options.why: Used the linear coefficients $6$ and $-10$ directly, giving centre $(-6, 10)$, instead of halving them to $(-3, 5)$.
Failed to square root $r^2 = 25$, using $25$ as the radius instead of $r = 5$.
Used the unhalved linear coefficients for the centre $(-6, 10)$ and also failed to square root $r^2 = 25$ to get $r = 5$.
